new_codes.definition: Named AI-use levels, categories or quantitative caps (e.g., 'AI Use Generally Permitted', per-assessment rules, <=15% or 1-3 lines of borrowed code). From PI scope addendum.
Provisions on AI for prose such as comments, documentation, drafts, changelogs, reports or notes, as opposed to code. From PI scope addendum.
Instructor or TA use of AI to grade or give feedback, and the related transparency, privacy and opt-out terms. From PI scope addendum.
Instructor use of AI to build course materials such as textbooks or examples. From PI scope addendum.
Named categories/levels/tiers of permitted AI use (from PI scope addendum).
AI use for prose: reports, documentation, comments, grammar/translation (from PI scope addendum).
Instructors using AI to create or generate course materials (from PI scope addendum).
Explicit tiers or levels of permitted AI use (e.g., restricted / limited / when instructed / all use). From PI scope addendum.
Provisions on AI for writing text (reports, documentation, grammar/spelling), as opposed to code. From PI scope addendum.
Instructor or staff use of AI or automated systems for grading, feedback or monitoring of student work. From PI scope addendum.
Provisions that let a student self-report or withdraw a submission involving misuse within a window, in exchange for a reduced penalty or no formal referral.
Named AI-use categories, levels or tiers (e.g., icon sets, 'AI for Support and Growth', appendix taxonomies) that courses select from or map assignments to. From the PI's scope addendum.
Provisions on AI for writing or editing text (reports, documentation, messages), as distinct from code. From the PI's scope addendum.
Instructor or TA use of AI to review, give feedback on, or score student work. From the PI's scope addendum.
Instructor use of AI to create or refine course materials, assignments or assessments. From the PI's scope addendum.
